name: colourful-text

frames.best_why: Every letter sits still and sharp in its own colour, with no blur from the animation cycle.

tagline: Each letter of a big heading pulses its own bright colour.
summary: A short phrase drawn one letter at a time, each character in a vivid rotating colour that bounces, swells and briefly blurs, with the palette reshuffling every few seconds.
appearance: A single bold sans-serif phrase on black, about one line wide, every letter a different saturated colour running from green through blue, purple and magenta to orange.
behaviour: Letters bounce up a few pixels, swell slightly and blur in and out on a staggered wave, then settle. Every five seconds the colours reshuffle and the whole word animates again.
demo_content: The words Hello World in large bold capitals.
search_phrases: each letter a different bright colour
playful title for a kids site
use_when: A short, playful headline should grab attention, such as a tagline or friendly greeting.
avoid_when: Long copy or serious brands: constant colour shifts and blur hurt readability and distract from the message.
customise: Only the phrase is a prop; the ten-colour palette, shuffle interval and per-letter motion are all fixed in the source.
weight_why: A span per letter with short transitions and a five-second timer.

a11y.note: Each letter is its own span, so screen readers may read it character by character, and the motion ignores reduced-motion.

issues: Mid-cycle every letter blurs heavily and the word becomes briefly unreadable.
Splitting the phrase into one span per letter can break copying and screen-reader reading.
polish_why: Vivid per-letter colour is fun and smooth; the blur phase briefly makes the word unreadable.
title: Colourful Text
